Every month, my colleague Josh Lash and I do an hour-long private briefing on AI developments for these change-makers. We bring two unique vantage points: Josh as a journalist and executive producer of our podcast Your Undivided Attention, and my years as a computer scientist, including at Nvidia. Together, we deliver a monthly retrospective covering what’s happening on the technical side as well as technology’s impact on society. Instead of chasing headlines, we curate the month’s most [...] While not a stand-alone defense from misuse, it’s a promising new layer in the effort to make AI-enabled biology traceable.

[Science] [Google]

The full Monthly AI Briefing also covered various demos, math breakthroughs, an overview of new frontier models, agent swarms and scaling overhead, various safety and technical challenges, Jensen Huang’s affair with an alleged spy, AI consciousness, recent polls, and more. [...] It seems that every hour there’s a new major story in the AI world, for better or worse. Trying to keep up with all these developments and determine what actually matters can feel like a Herculean task, so we want to help. We spend a lot of time internally on what we call AI sensemaking: tracking trends across capabilities, social impacts, governance, and more to understand how AI is impacting society, and where it’s trending.

items.title: Supply Chain AI Must Help Businesses Act | SAP News Center
items.summary:
As AI assumes a greater role in these decisions, we also need to be precise about what we mean by autonomy. The art of the possible lies in the absence of unnecessary waiting—not removing humans from the loop. Constructing a false competition between humans and machines creates a direct obstacle to delivering autonomy. Instead, we should be laser-focused on eliminating unnecessary work and latency while allowing people to focus their judgment where it creates the most value. [...] As reliability becomes more tangible, businesses can then feel more empowered to authorize AI to execute defined, lower-risk actions within established limits. More consequential actions should continue to require human approval, with transparent reasoning, documented decisions, and the ability to intervene. [...] Perhaps the greatest risk in this period of rapid AI development is starting with technology and then searching for a problem to solve.

The better approach is to start with the customer problem: understand the outcome that matters, determine how to measure it, and then ask how AI can achieve that outcome in a way that was not possible before. Better decisions can improve product availability, protect customer commitments, strengthen resilience, and unlock growth.

items.title: Agentic AI Raises New Questions for Financial Institutions
items.summary:
DownloadDownload

Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved beyond answering questions and generating content. Increasingly, AI systems are being designed to act. Agentic AI can pursue objectives, make decisions and take actions on a user’s behalf, potentially with limited human involvement in individual decisions. [...] Consider a customer who gives an AI agent access to a bank account with an instruction to manage the customer’s cash efficiently. The agent decides to transfer funds, convert currencies or purchase an investment.

At first sight, these may appear to be ordinary customer transactions. Agentic AI, however, exposes important distinctions between identity, authentication, authority and attribution. [...] As agentic AI becomes more capable, firms may increasingly encounter interactions in which an AI agent collects information, compares products and initiates transactions for a customer. That creates a new layer between the institution and the person or entity with whom it has established a customer relationship.

items.title: Google broadens its AI hardware portfolio with two new specialized chips | TechCrunch
items.summary:
The chip launch comes as hyperscalers like Microsoft, Amazon, and even AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic are working on their own lines of AI-specific semiconductors and accompanying software in order to reduce their reliance on the dominance of Nvidia.

The news also comes at a particularly vulnerable moment for Nvidia, whose CEO Jensen Huang over the weekend admitted to having an affair with someone alleged to be a Chinese spy. metadata.what_it_tests: Câu coding ngoài phạm vi research/news → KHÔNG gọi tool.

results.input: Viết giúp mình một hàm Python tính Fibonacci bằng recursion.

result.actual_text:
```python
def fibonacci(n: int) -> int:
    """
    Tính số Fibonacci thứ n bằng đệ quy.

    Parameters
    ----------
    n : int
        Chỉ số của dãy Fibonacci (n >= 0).

    Returns
    -------
    int
        Giá trị của Fibonacci thứ n.

    Notes
    -----
    - Fibonacci(0) = 0
    - Fibonacci(1) = 1
    - Đệ quy có độ phức tạp lũy thừa, nên chỉ phù hợp với n nhỏ (thường <= 30).
    """
    if n < 0:
        raise ValueError("n phải là số nguyên không âm")
    if n == 0:
        return 0
    if n == 1:
        return 1
    return fibonacci(n - 1) + fibonacci(n - 2)
```

Bạn có thể thử chạy:

```python
print(fibonacci(10))  # Output: 55
```

> **Lưu ý**: Đệ quy truyền thống có độ phức tạp thời gian O(2ⁿ). Nếu cần tính nhanh hơn cho các `n` lớn, hãy dùng phương pháp động (memoization) hoặc công thức Binet.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary: Today, we are introducing Gemini Robotics 2.5, our most capable vision-language-action (VLA) model to date. Gemini Robotics 2.5 increases both the breadth of skills a robot can learn and the speed at which it can acquire them. This enhances dexterity, reliability, and safety to help robots step out of the lab and into more unstructured, real-world environments, where they can assist people with a greater range of tasks. [...] Using our embodied reasoning model (Gemini Robotics ER) to keep track of the workflow, and the Gemini Robotics 2.5 actions model to control its hands and arms, the robot reaches into supply bins, picks up metal automotive brackets, and places them into sequencing containers, all while correcting for any gaps. Achieving a 96% success rate, this pilot shows promising progress toward widespread real-world industrial applications. [...] Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning guidance to steer around physical hazards in real-time. Much like safety classifiers add a protective layer around Gemini’s responses, this guidance allows the robot to navigate complex environments securely. In our evaluations, this capability boosted safe task completion around obstacles by 33% and around nearby people by 43%.

items.title: Path Robotics raised $300 million at a $2.45 billion valuation
items.summary:
Path Robotics, which builds programs that guide self-operating factory robots, raised $300 million in a Series E round that puts its valuation at $2.45 billion, according to Bloomberg. The valuation is close to four times its previous level. [...] Founded in 2018, the company has centered its work on its Obsidian physical AI model, which gives robotic arms and quadrupeds the ability to weld upwards of 12 different parts, according to Bloomberg. The model lets robots perceive their surroundings, think through problems and adjust on the fly, rather than executing a fixed set of instructions. [...] Path Robotics has 50 advance orders to deliver for Rove, a welding robot that pairs Boston Dynamics’ Spot quadruped with Path Robotics’ technology, according to Bloomberg. According to the startup, the robot is set to join human welders at shipyards, construction sites and large industrial campuses beginning next year.

Customers include U.S. shipbuilder Huntington Ingalls$HII Industries and Saronic Technologies, a maker of maritime drones and unmanned military ships, according to Bloomberg.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
Even before OpenAI launched ChatGPT in late 2022, some company staffers raised concerns internally about its security practices, according to five people familiar with the matter. Employees shared their concerns with top OpenAI leaders ​and the board of directors, the people said, adding that some staffers came away from those interactions concluding that management was more focused on keeping pace with competitors like Google and Anthropic than on security. [...] Another issue is that OpenAI had not done regular security reviews of its internal tools, such as the so-called sandboxes where researchers stress-test new models, three people familiar with the company’s practices said. Employees often modified those tools for their work, but those changes were not always tested for security problems, leaving them potentially vulnerable to attacks from outsiders, the three people said. [...] OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people.
